title: Manual Bit-Shifting for Division / Multiplication
pattern: Using bit-shift operators (`<<`, `>>`) instead of normal multiplication/division operators (`*`, `/`) by powers of two to "speed up math."
why_bad: Modern optimizing compilers automatically convert multiplication and division by powers of two to optimal bit-shift assembly instructions. Manual bit-shifting severely degrades code readability and obscures mathematical intentions for zero performance gain [348, 430].
detection: Bit-shift operations on integers where standard mathematical multiplication or division operators are semantically intended.
counterexample: Explicit low-level bit manipulation protocols, cryptographic hashing, or packet parsing. `Context-dependent`.
source: *Code Complete*, Section 25.3 (p. 348); *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 1 (p. 430).
